text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo believes he has found a player who can perform the role of a winger, the rarest of species in modern football.
The veteran coach spoke glowingly on Wednesday of 19-year-old attacking midfielder Denilson, who has transformed two recent games for Brazil after coming on as substitute.
The discovery of Denilson -- full name Denilson de Oliveira -- has more than made up for the team's shaky defence.

Zagallo is still searching for the ideal partnership at the back and announced yet another change on Wednesday, with Goncalves relacing Celio Silva as Aldair's partner at the heart of the defence for Thursday's Copa America match against Colombia.
When Denilson came on in the second half of Brazil's match against Italy in the Tournoi de France earlier this month, his surging runs down the left helped them turn a 3-1 deficit into a 3-3 draw.

On Monday, Brazil were completely overrun by Mexico in the first half of their Copa America match and went in 2-0 down at halftime. Denilson, who plays for Sao Paulo, came on at the re-start and a revitalised team bounced back to win 3-2.
"Brazil always used to have exceptional wingers, who were feared by the opponents," said Zagallo, modestly excluding himself from his list of the best ones, which was naturally topped by Garrincha.

"They seem to have disappeared from the Brazilian game. But Denilson has excellent organic condition, he can perform a double function on the field and he has the characterisitcs of a left winger. It's important to have a resurgance of this type of player."
Denilson made his first impact with Sao Paulo, where he was raised, in 1993 when he scored a brilliant individual goal in a South American Conmebol Cup match.
He has been playing regularly for the Sao Paulo team for the last 18 months and was rewarded when he was picked for a friendly against Cameroon last year, the first of five full caps to date.

There were some words of caution from Zagallo, however. "He's still a young player and he mustn't get carried away with all the praise that is being heaped on him." And, as if to bring Denilson down to earth, he added a criticsim: "Sometimes he exaggerates with his dribbling."

Zagallo, who rarely picks out individuals for comment, confirmed that Denilson would keep his place in the team for Thursday's group C match against Colombia at the expense of Djalminha, the man he replaced against Mexico.
Brazil have already qualified for the quarter-finals by winning their first two games and need a point on Thursday to win their group and make sure they continue in Santa Cruz.
The big worry has been the defence, which conceeded four goals in a recent friendly against Norway, three against Italy and two more against Mexico.
Zagallo began Brazil's series of fixtures with Celio Silva and Marcio Santos at the back against Norway, then switched to Celio Santos and Aldair.

In the first Copa America game against Costa Rica, he tried Goncalves with Aldair, then reverted to Aldair and Celio Silva against Mexico. The recall of Goncalves follows a horrendous mix-up between the two for Mexico's second goal on Monday.
"I said we would use this trip to make observations," he said cagily. "At the end of our trip, we will reach conclusions."
